purpose: TOPIC_NEARBY_TEXT_AND_ALL_OPTIONS_ONLY; no key or review judgement

records.stem:
Case A: A Board inspector arrives without advance notice. The pharmacy refuses access because it completed its annual self-inspection last week.

Case B: A pharmacy changes its MOR and keeps the old self-inspection file without conducting the applicable event-triggered review.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Only the annual calendar date can trigger a required self-inspection.
The MOR's absence automatically permits refusal of all inspection records.
An annual self-inspection does not replace the Board's inspection authority.
Self-inspection forms may be discarded once the next month's schedule is posted.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy receives a statement of deficiencies and submits a vague promise to improve, without responsible persons or implementation dates.

Case B: The Board finds the plan unacceptable and returns it for revision. The pharmacy waits for the next annual inspection before responding.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The revised-plan deadline is the date of the next annual inspection.
The written plan should address each violation with corrective actions, timing, and responsibility.
Submitting a plan automatically establishes that the pharmacy is compliant.
Every initial plan has an unchangeable 90-day submission period.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacist practices while unable to exercise reasonable skill and safety, despite an employer's approval to remain on duty.

Case B: A reviewer assumes that receiving treatment for a medical condition automatically proves unsafe practice and warrants the same disciplinary conclusion.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Employer approval does not excuse unsafe or impaired professional practice.
Only medication dispensing errors can support Board discipline.
Conviction means only a final sentence of incarceration for this regulatory purpose.
Receiving medical treatment automatically establishes professional impairment.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacist receives an advisory letter and describes it as identical to a formal reprimand on a credentialing form.

Case B: Another pharmacist signs a consent agreement that includes practice restrictions and assumes that an agreed resolution can never be disciplinary.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Probation necessarily cancels the license permanently.
Every investigative conference is already the final merits hearing.
Every consent agreement is nondisciplinary because the licensee agreed to it.
An advisory letter is distinguished from formal disciplinary action.

records.stem:
Case A: The Board finds documentary evidence of an immediate serious public threat and takes summary suspension action before a final merits hearing.

Case B: In a separate matter, a cease-and-desist or quarantine notice limits pharmacy operations to address an immediate danger.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Cease-and-desist and summary-suspension hearings necessarily use the same clock.
The summary-action limited hearing is ordinarily deferred for 90 days.
Summary action can precede the final hearing when the specified public-threat conditions are met.
A nondisciplinary interim restriction is optional for the pharmacy to obey.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy submits a waiver petition based only on cost savings and starts disregarding the regulation while the application is pending.

Case B: A pharmacy with a granted state regulatory waiver assumes that the waiver also removes federal controlled-substance requirements.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Cost savings alone automatically establish all waiver criteria.
A pending petition is not a granted waiver and does not itself excuse compliance.
A state Board waiver automatically supersedes applicable federal law.
A granted waiver lasts for the lifetime of the pharmacy without an expiration review.
